name: Adult-onset immunodeficiency with anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies
aliases: Adult-onset immunodeficiency syndrome with anti-interferon-gamma antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for adult-onset immunodeficiency with anti-IFN-γ autoantibodies

criteria.description: Detection of neutralizing anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies in serum
Clinical evidence of recurrent or disseminated infections caused by nontuberculous mycobacteria or other opportunistic intracellular pathogens
Exclusion of primary immunodeficiencies, HIV infection, and other secondary immunodeficiencies
Elevated serum immunoglobulin levels and abnormal cytokine profiles supportive of immune dysregulation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of neutralizing anti-IFN-γ autoantibodies plus recurrent or disseminated opportunistic infections with exclusion of other immunodeficiencies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on serologic testing and clinical presentation; genetic testing may be used to exclude primary immunodeficiencies.

pathognomonic.notes: Often involves lymph nodes, lungs, and skin

common.notes: Due to chronic infections and immune activation

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary infiltrates due to opportunistic infections

occasional.notes: Usually secondary to mycobacterial or Salmonella infections
searchTerms: bone infection from spread of germs

occasional.notes: Due to chronic infection and immune activation

searchTerms: high levels of antibodies in blood

rare.symptomName: Neurological manifestations secondary to CNS infections
rare.notes: Rare but reported in severe disseminated infections
searchTerms: nerve issues due to central infections

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment due to immune complex deposition
searchTerms: kidney impairment due to immune complexes

laboratory: Detection of neutralizing anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies by ELISA or functional assays
imaging: Chest radiographs or CT showing pulmonary infiltrates or lymphadenopathy
MRI or CT evidence of osteomyelitis or abscess formation
genetic: No known monogenic mutations; genetic testing used to exclude primary immunodeficiencies
other: Microbiological cultures positive for nontuberculous mycobacteria or Salmonella species

distinguishingFeatures: Positive acid-fast bacilli staining for Mycobacterium tuberculosis

redFlags: Recurrent or disseminated nontuberculous mycobacterial infections
Failure to respond to standard antimicrobial therapy
references: Browne SK. Anti-interferon-γ autoantibodies: a cause of adult-onset immunodeficiency associated with severe opportunistic infections. Clin Infect Dis. 2014;58(5):646-654.

Chi CY, Su CT, Hsiao CF, et al. Clinical manifestations and outcomes of adult-onset immunodeficiency with anti-interferon-γ autoantibodies: a multicenter study. Clin Infect Dis. 2016;62(10):1350-1358.
